Andy Taylor, who has died aged 65, was the wild boy of Duran Duran.
In the early 1980s, the pop legends sold over 100 million records and dominated the charts in both Britain and the United States.
But success came at a cost. For Taylor, global superstardom became a cocaine and alcohol fuelled nightmare that left him burnt out and battling clinical depression.
"For sure, we paraded around in our fast cars with beautiful models on yachts in the south of France without needing to pay the bill," he later wrote.
Andrew Taylor was born in North Tyneside on 16 February 1961.
Home was Cullercoats, a coastal village near Whitley Bay where many people, including his uncles, depended on the sea for their livelihoods.
At first, it was a happy childhood. There was church on Sunday with his parents, Ronnie and Blanche, followed by games of football on the beach with younger brother Ronnie junior.
On Christmas Day, his extended family would belt out Bing Crosby hits around the piano.
Andy Taylor's childhood was blighted when his mother abandoned the family without explanation
The 11-year-old returned home to find his father in the kitchen, silently weeping. Taylor's mother, it seemed, had simply disappeared. There wasn't even a note.
"It was like a guillotine had suddenly come rushing down," he recalled. It "sliced everything apart without explanation as to why I was guilty".
After that, occasional meetings with his mother were chilly encounters with no explanation offered. Taylor never discovered why she had left.
Having worked hard to pass his 11-plus exams, Taylor rapidly went off the rails.
He skipped school and spent many days in remote caves on the beach, drinking cider and smoking dried banana skins. He'd heard absurd rumours this would get him high.
Salvation lay in a guitar he found hidden in his father's cupboard and a BBC Two programme that taught him the basic chords.
Andy Taylor's earliest performances were in working men's clubs in the north-east of England
By the age of 16, he was working on a building site and playing in a band.
Taylor and his friends performed at working men's clubs across the north-east of England, often providing musical accompaniment for strippers.
A contract to provide entertainment for American troops in Germany included a clause stipulating that he did six hours a night on stage.
On his return, Taylor saw an advert seeking a "livewire guitarist" for a new band based in the West Midlands.
He called the number and "made that fateful train journey to Birmingham".
Duran Duran, named after a character in Jane Fonda's space-sex movie Barbarella, were to be based in a club called the Rum Runner.
On arrival, he met bassist John Taylor and drummer Roger Taylor - all unrelated.
Keyboardist Nick Rhodes followed and, after a short search, Simon Le Bon, the lead singer, appeared "looking like an Elvis who'd been to the chip shop".
Andy Taylor's initial impression of Simon Le Bon was that he looked like Elvis who'd been to a chip shop
They didn't waste time. Within six weeks, the group had pulled together enough material for an album.
Andy Taylor's musical challenge was to work out how his guitar fitted a post-punk age of electronic music, while Le Bon's lyrics and melody skated over the top.
A record deal with EMI gave the group the production support they needed.
Planet Earth was released on 21 February 1981. It raced towards the top 10, winning them a coveted slot on Top of the Pops.
Six months later, Girls on Film reached number five in the UK charts.
The New Romantic revolution, as much about fashion as music, was under way.
The boys discovered that their Antony Price suits and make-up gave them something to talk about with girls in the clubs.
And there were soon girls everywhere, thanks to a marketing campaign that pushed the band heavily in teen magazines.
After one US concert, the band swept the stage and supposedly counted 2,000 teddy bears, 150 pairs of knickers, 300 bras and dozens of hotel room keys that had been thrown from the crowd.
Andy Taylor said life with Duran Duran was like entering Narnia in The Lion, The Witch and The Wardrobe
"We were just working-class escapists who wanted to live out our dreams," explained Taylor. "We didn't want to be like UB40 and The Specials singing about unemployment and urban decay."
Duran Duran embarked on exhausting foreign tours to drive sales, and their flamboyant videos, made at huge cost, played constantly on MTV in the US.
A bandmate pushed Taylor off a yacht while shooting the video for Rio, and he nearly drowned off the Caribbean coast amid a swarm of poisonous jellyfish.
In Sri Lanka, the group was forced to flee when 4,000 furious monks objected to their using a holy site as a backdrop to Hungry Like the Wolf.
Then, having smoked dope and drunk a bottle of Jack Daniel's, Taylor climbed a tree with his guitar for a spectacular shot.
He fell into a muddy lagoon that was used by local elephants as a latrine and spent four days in hospital recovering from a tropical infection.
By now, Taylor's original £50-a-week retainer from EMI was a distant memory.
He shared a flat in Moseley with Le Bon, took prodigious quantities of cocaine, and worked his way through the flocks of page three girls who frequented the Rum Runner.
Andy Taylor married Tracey Wilson on Hollywood's Sunset Strip in 1982
Then he met Tracey Wilson, a level-headed hair salon manager.
Initially, she had doubts about becoming romantically involved with a self-confessed womanising, drug-taking guitarist.
She was eventually persuaded and, on his 21st birthday, Taylor proposed. The couple remained together for more than 40 years and had four children.
Famously, Duran Duran were Princess Diana's favourite band. This too, came with risks.
In June 1983, the IRA tried to assassinate the Prince and Princess of Wales while they watched the group perform live at Tottenham Court Road's Dominion Theatre.
The plot, which involved planting a bomb in the toilets, was stopped by British intelligence.
Fortunately, the IRA man sent to plant the device turned out to be a double agent, who tipped off MI5 and fled to Paris.
Princess Diana met Duran Duran 1983. Unbeknownst to Andy Taylor (far right) the IRA were plotting to bomb the venue
The same year, Is There Something I Should Know? became Duran Duran's fastest-selling song to date.
The Reflex, which their record company initially refused to release, also topped the charts on both sides of the Atlantic.
The American press called them the Fab Five, in comparison to the Beatles, and their vast earnings caused them to become tax exiles.
For Andy Taylor, foreign tours had become increasingly drug-fuelled with so-called "rock docs" injecting him with chemicals to get through sets.
The constant use of cocaine made him nervy and irrational. The BBC threatened to ban him from their Saturday Superstore programme when he swore at a caller.
Headlines about Taylor's drug use at the Rum Runner damaged the band's hitherto squeaky-clean image.
In Birmingham, the club was suddenly served with a compulsory purchase order by the council and bulldozed.
Their Wild Boys video featured Simon Le Bon strapped to a huge waterwheel. But it was Andy Taylor who felt as if he was drowning.
Andy Taylor (sitting in a cardboard box) and Simon Le Bon behind the scenes at Live Aid in 1985
As a guitarist, he wanted to make records with a harder rock edge, which led to The Power Station - a band he put together with Robert Palmer while killing time between Duran Duran tours.
But it was his lifestyle that was worrying him. After years of living on Big Macs and cocaine, he knew he was heading for a breakdown.
After Live Aid in 1985, the constant bickering between members of the band led to a prolonged separation.
When they ran out of money, Duran Duran's original line-up reformed to work on new projects.
They continued to sell plenty of tickets for live shows to die-hard fans, but new records had disappointing sales.

1Password says the security breach didn’t compromise its vaults, but didn’t mention how many customers were affected.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
1Password says a hacker stole customer names and email addresses after gaining access to its backend systems. The breach didn’t expose passwords or other information stored in customer vaults, but could put users at risk of phishing attempts, according to a post disclosing the incident . It’s unclear how many users are affected.
The password manager began investigating the incident on November 19th, after an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. Using the compromised account, the hacker accessed 1Password’s source code and pushed malicious code to backend services to download customer data. Along with customer names and emails, the leaked data included public keys, as well as account and user identifiers.
It also included tokens from certain emailed invitation or account recovery links. According to 1Password, attackers can’t use tokens alone to gain access to an account, as they would need to pair them with a single-sign-on method or a six-digit numeric code sent to a user’s email. 1Password has since lengthened the codes it sends to users to 10 alphanumeric characters to make them harder to guess.
The password manager also disabled the affected GitHub account, rotated internal credentials compromised by the breach, and added a new detection system for similar attacks. It warns customers about potential phishing attempts as well, saying phony emails, texts, or calls may reference 1Password invitations or account recovery attempts. The company says it will never ask customers for their account password or Secret Key, and that users should only enter this information into the official 1Password app or website.

Pitt filed the lawsuit against Jolie in 2022 after she sold her stake in Château Miraval, saying she broke their agreement not to sell their interests
Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have settled a years-long legal battle over their French winery, according to a joint statement from the former Hollywood couple.
“We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” representatives for Jolie and Pitt said in a statement. “Any comments in media stories attributed to ‘sources’ are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us.”
Both sides have moved to dismiss claims against each other. The terms of the agreement were not made public.
The couple had bought a controlling interest in Château Miraval in 2008, and married there in 2014.
Jolie initiated divorce proceedings in 2016, and the couple was declared legally single in 2019, although their divorce settlement continued to play out until 2024 . Jolie was cleared to sell her share in 2021 for $164m (£125.06m) before their wider financial settlement was finalized.
Pitt filed the lawsuit against Jolie in February 2022, after the actor sold her stake in the French winery to the Stoli Group, a spirits maker controlled by oligarch Yuri Shefler. In the suit, Pitt said Jolie had broken their agreement not to sell their interests in the winery without the other’s consent after she sold her stake to the Russian businessman.
In October 2022, Jolie filed a counter lawsuit against Pitt, which for the first time described alleged abusive behavior that led to their divorce. The actor’s attorneys said negotiations for Jolie to sell her share in the winery to Pitt broke down over his demand that she sign “a nondisclosure agreement that would have contractually prohibited her from speaking outside of court about Pitt’s physical and emotional abuse of her and their children”. Pitt denied the accusations.

Watch: Andy Taylor tells the BBC about his cancer diagnosis in 2023
Andy Taylor, the guitarist for the pop group Duran Duran, has died at the age of 65.
Born in Tynemouth, he co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits, including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film; and also worked with artists like Robert Palmer, Rod Stewart and Belinda Carlisle.
In a statement, his bandmates said Taylor had fought "a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer" and "passed away peacefully at home, surrounded by his family, on Monday 23 November".
His wife, Tracey, said the musician "was the rock of our family", adding: "We will miss him every single day".
Andy Taylor: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a Wild Boy on stage and off
The son of a fisherman, Taylor taught himself guitar, bass, and drums and began playing professionally at age 13.
He played with several bands around the UK before answering a music paper advertisement for a "live-wire guitarist", which led to his audition for Duran Duran in Birmingham in April 1980.
The group went on to achieve global fame through the New Romantic movement, which combined slick, melodic synth-pop with aspirational music videos and chiselled good looks.
Andy Taylor's guitar riffs powered some of Duran Duran's best-known songs
Taylor's guitar lines - full of glassy, powerful riffs - were often a highlight of their songs, from the choppy opening of Girls on Film to the sleazy scuzz of Hungry Like The Wolf.
"Andy was there at the very beginning of our story," said his bandmates Simon Le Bon, Nick Rhodes, John Taylor and Roger Taylor (his bandmates were unrelated, despite sharing the same last name).
"From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music.
"His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.
"Our thoughts are with his wife Tracey, his children Georgina, Isabella, Bethany and Andrew, and grandson Albie. They all loved him deeply and we ask that their privacy be respected at this very difficult time."
Taylor quit Duran Duran at the height of their fame in 1985, but rejoined the band several times in the 2000s and contributed to their most recent album, Danse Macabre
Duran Duran were one of the biggest pop acts of the 1980s, and its five members became global hearththrobs.
Their indelible hooks and airbrushed music videos found a natural home on the newly launched MTV, giving their career a huge boost in the US.
They became so popular in the States that the press labeled them the leaders of a "Second British Invasion" of the charts - alongside groups like Spandau Ballet, Human League and Eurythmics.
During a hiatus in 1984, Andy and John Taylor enlisted Robert Palmer for their successful but short-lived side project the Power Station.
Duran Duran bridged the sounds of pop, funk, disco, punk and new wave with a sound that remains indelibly tied to the 1980s
The following year, the guitarist decided to quit Duran Duran, after a miserable experience performing at Live Aid.
"We'd reached rock bottom and we had absolutely nothing to say to each other," he wrote in his autobiography, Wild Boy.
"We drove to the venue through streets packed with excited rock fans, but inside the bus the atmosphere was as if we were on a way to a funeral."
He went on to play on Robert Palmer's Addicted To Love, and released a solo album, Thunder, in 1987.
After a period writing and producing albums for other artists, he rejoined Duran Duran in 2000, lasting for just one album (2004's Astronaut) before parting ways again.
In 2022, when the band were inducted to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Taylor was notably absent from the ceremony, despite public plans for a reunion.
When the group took the stage, singer Simon Le Bon read a letter from the guitarist, in which he revealed his diagnosis with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer.
Nonetheless, he contributed to the following year's Halloween-themed album Danse Macabre, marking his final collaboration with the band.
Taylor (second left) married his wife Tracey at the Chateau Marmont hotel in Los Angeles in 1982
"Andy never took the easy musical route," said Le Bon in a personal statement marking his friend's death.
"His overdrive, overdrove us into being the only funk/rock/punk band in the New Romantic movement, with songs that still survive, decades later.
"There's a massive Andy Taylor shaped hole in my heart. It'll never close up; I won't let it. I will miss him & love him for all my days."
Taylor is survived by his wife, Tracey, a hairstylist he met during the early days of Duran Duran, and whom he married in 1982.
"For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first," she wrote in her statement.
"Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home."
She continued: "Andy faced the last few years with so much courage and determination. He never gave up, fighting until the very end, never losing his love of life.
"The kindness and support shown to him by fans from all over the world throughout his illness brought him immense comfort and strength, and for that we will always be grateful."

Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have settled a long-running legal battle over her sale of a stake in their French vineyard, which unfolded amid a bitter divorce.
"We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further," said the Hollywood stars' representatives in a joint statement.
They bought a controlling interest in Château Miraval in 2008 and wed there six years later.
In the lawsuit, Pitt , 62, argued that Jolie , 51, acted without his permission in selling her share in the winery to a Russian oligarch. She counter-sued, accusing Pitt of drunkenly attacking her and their children on a flight, prompting her to file for divorce in 2016.
The settlement announced on Wednesday resolves both of their respective legal actions.
"Any comments in media stories attributed to 'sources' are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us," said the statement from their representatives.
Pitt's lawsuit had accused Jolie of seeking "to inflict harm" on him when she sold her stake in their co-owned vineyard, which he claimed had forced him to partner with "a stranger with poisonous associations and intentions".
The Fight Club star said he and Jolie had agreed not to sell their stakes in the venue without the permission of the other.
It was alleged that Jolie had sold her share to a Luxembourg-based spirits manufacturer controlled by Russian oligarch Yuri Shefler, without Pitt's knowledge.
Jolie hit back with her own lawsuit, accusing Pitt of grabbing her by the head and attacking two of their children during a 2016 private jet flight trip.
Pitt also verbally abused and poured alcohol on his family during the flight from France to Los Angeles, her lawsuit had alleged.
Her lawyers alleged Pitt began shouting, accusing her of being "too deferential" to their six children - aged eight to 15 at the time.
Pitt was not charged following a police investigation into the incident and he denied the allegations.
They reached a divorce settlement late last year after an eight-year legal battle.
It is understood that Pitt's litigation with Stoli Group, a beverage company owned by the Russian oligarch, is ongoing.
At the time of their 2014 marriage, Pitt and Jolie were among the most lucrative names in Hollywood.
They met on the set of the 2005 film Mr and Mrs Smith and were soon dubbed Brangelina by the press.
The marriage was Pitt's second after a relationship with Friends star Jennifer Aniston.
It was Jolie's third, after actors Billy Bob Thornton and Jonny Lee Miller.
Jolie adopted her first child, Maddox, from Cambodia in 2002 a few months after he was born. Pitt later adopted him after he and Jolie had begun their relationship.
In 2005, the pair adopted daughter Zahara from Ethiopia when she was a few months old.
The couple's first biological child, Shiloh, was born in Namibia in 2006.
Their son Pax was adopted at the age of three from Vietnam in 2007, and twins Knox and Vivienne were born in 2008.
Since the couple split, four of the six children have legally changed their last name to Jolie rather than Jolie-Pitt, according to court filings citied by Hollywood press.

Record-breaking king tides have prompted west coast authorities to warn residents to stay away from beaches
The US west coast has seen record-breaking tides this week and authorities have urged residents to avoid beaches, but not everyone is heeding those warnings.
In Cannon Beach, Oregon , viral footage showed a man and his dog nearly getting swept away by a so-called king tide on Tuesday morning. The man had been standing on a staircase holding his leashed dog, who was walking in the sand, when the water suddenly surged, knocking him to his feet.
They ultimately escaped without injury, according to the Cannon Beach police department. Earlier that morning, police had cited the same man for driving on the shoreline. He had reportedly “indicated” to an officer he wanted to get a better look at the high tides.
Other footage captured around Cannon Beach on Tuesday morning showed a jogger narrowly avoiding a major wave, while another stood amid the wave seemingly filming.
King tides are the highest tide cycles of the year. This winter, conditions caused by the super El Niño have pushed these tides to record levels, contributing to widespread flooding, powerful waves and coastal erosion.
The Cannon Beach police department advised residents to stay off beaches and keep pets away from the water.
“King tides are an impressive natural phenomenon, but no photograph, video or closer look is worth risking your life, the life of your pet or the lives of the first responders who may be called upon to rescue you,” the police department said in a statement.
A coastal flood advisory is in effect for the region through Thursday, according to the National Weather Service, as “king tides, elevated seas, and the arrival of fresh swells likely lead to tidal overflow”.

High king tides threaten California coastline, flood communities
Coastal areas of California are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak in the state during the US Thanksgiving holiday.
Water levels across the US state's vast coastline could reach over 8ft (2.4 metres) in some areas on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the National Weather Service (NWS) - breaking records set just last month.
The NWS has warned parts of California could face major coastal flooding, which is likely to be significant in low-lying areas. There have already been some reports of flooding.
Meanwhile, storms are also forecast for the Pacific Northwest, including the Canadian province of British Columbia, and eastern parts of the US.
Portions of a pier in northern California came crashing down into the ocean on Wednesday as high tides and strong waves battered the structure, video showed.
Beachgoers have been advised to stay away from the water's edge as large waves could suddenly form. Such waves could be damaging to piers and jetties, and could capsize small vessels, the NWS warned.
Flooding has already been reported in the San Francisco Bay Area.
In San Diego, a high tide of 8 ft 11in was recorded on Wednesday morning local time - potentially breaking the record for highest tide measured in the area, which was just set late last month at 7.98ft.
In Los Angeles, the tide on Wednesday was thought to be as high 8.19 - the record for the city that was set only weeks ago 27 October when parts of the California coast experienced flooding.
Recently set high tide records were also broken in Santa Barbara and La Jolla, according to preliminary data.
King tides are the highest predicted tide of the year and are above the highest water level reached at high tide on an average day.
While they typically occur once or twice a year in most coastal areas, they are happening more frequently in some as sea levels rise. These king tides are being strengthened by the strongest El Niño weather pattern on record.
Storm systems are also expected to impact the US through the Thanksgiving holiday - one affecting the Pacific Northwest and another the eastern part of the country, the US National Weather Service said.
On the east coast, a developing Nor'easter storm is expected to bring heavy rain, strong winds, and coastal flooding.
Major impacts are expected to begin on Wednesday across the southeast, and move northward Wednesday night and on Thursday, the NWS said.
"Those along the eastern seaboard can expect gusty, possibly damaging winds, heavy rain, and major coastal and marine impacts," it added.
The developing storm system could bring about one to four inches rain along America's east coast and a peak of four to six inches in coastal North Carolina.
The US department store chain Macy's has postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York, which was due to take place on Thursday, until Saturday because of severe weather - the first time this has happened.
The stormy weather on both coasts could disrupt travel for millions of people.
The American Automobile Association (AAA) has predicted that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles (80km) from home for Thanksgiving between Tuesday 24 November and Monday 30 November.
Officials have also issued a flood warning along Vancouver's coastline in Canada's most western province of British Columbia.
Residents were urged to take "immediate action to protect life and property", a weather warning from Environment and Climate Change Canada said.
King tides were expected to potentially increase already high water levels there too.

Beaches close as Los Angeles and La Jolla see all-time high tides and big waves batter landmark pier in Pacifica
Super El Niño weather brought record-breaking high tides up and down the California coast on Wednesday, sending seawater rushing into beachside communities and flooding roads and businesses.
As big waves battered the coast, the tip of a landmark pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, was slammed into the sea, local news outlets reported . The pier, which had once housed a favorite local cafe , had previously suffered structural damage and had been closed to the public, the San Francisco Chronicle reported , and collapsed after contact with ocean swells 12 times stronger than on an average November day.
Los Angeles and Santa Barbara tied or broke all-time high tide records on Wednesday, at 8.19 and 8.21ft, respectively, according to the National Weather Service (NWS). La Jolla, California, just north of San Diego, also set an all-time high tide record of 8.11ft (2.5 meters), according to the NWS, while preliminary data suggested that tides in Monterey, south of San Francisco, might also have set an all-time record at 8.03ft .
The city of Monterey closed multiple beaches to the public over safety concerns, with closures lasting until Friday. Beaches in Santa Cruz county were also closed.
“That sun may be out, but the beach and surf zone remain dangerous,” NWS San Francisco warned, citing waves around the San Francisco Bay area as high as 24ft.
“This is a preview of things to come,” California’s governor, Gavin Newsom, said in a San Francisco press conference about Wednesday’s flooding. “That’s why it’s so important that we not just situationally address and reflect on moments like this, but sustainably get under the hood and try to solve for some of these things.”
In Pacifica, giant waves and tide waters swept over beaches and piers, flooding coastal roads including Highway 1 near the famous local landmark Taco Bell Cantina, America’s poshest Taco Bell. (The iconic restaurant was unharmed by the tides, NBC Bay Area reported .)
“This El Niño is unprecedented with its strength,” the San Mateo county supervisor Ray Mueller told the Los Angeles Times . “For this to be happening when it is a beautiful day on the coast side today, in clear sunshine and no wind, is really significant.”
Multiple coastal homes in Sunset Beach, in Orange county, had flooded, the Los Angeles Times reported , but a local fire chief said the overall damage had been mitigated by how aggressively local homeowners had fortified their homes in advance.
Low-lying coastal roads around the Bay Area also saw flooding, including a stretch of road near the Golden Gate Bridge, which was temporarily closed, the Chronicle reported.
However, most of the state avoided the worst-case scenario – coastal flooding amplified by intense winter rainstorms.
“We’re past high tide, and San Francisco has made it through the worst of this round of king tides,” mayor Daniel Lurie said in a social media statement just after noon local time, saying officials were “only aware of minimal impacts across the city”.
Local officials had been preparing for weeks for the risk that flooding would disrupt travel during Thanksgiving week, one of the busiest times of the year. Experts warn that flooding risk will only worsen in the next two months.
Flooding risk at the San Francisco international airport, a major transit hub situated on low-lying coastal land, had been of particular concern. At least three airlines offered free trip changes to travelers whose journeys took them through San Francisco on Wednesday, the San Francisco Chronicle reported .
But the airport announced at noon that “We’re in the clear,” and said it was deactivating its emergency operations center after avoiding any impact from the high tides on Tuesday and Wednesday.
On the north coast, the NWS reported that Humboldt Bay saw its second highest tide on record, and advised residents to prepare for major coastal flooding in low lying areas. The county sheriff warned the public to stay away from beaches during the storm.
A local news outlet in Oregon shared a video on Tuesday that illustrated the risk of the west coast’s high-tide surf, showing a man and his dog almost getting swept away by unexpectedly high waves during the king tides in Cannon Beach, Oregon. Both man and dog escaped without injury, police told KVAL News .
The California governor’s office of emergency services deployed crews and equipment around the state to assist with storm response. In the Bay Area, crews could be seen preparing sandbags to help protect buildings from flooding.
California’s flooding risk this week is the result of a combination of factors, some of them driven by this year’s super El Niño weather, including the lingering effects of the massive Kelvin wave that traveled up California’s coast. The overlap of unusually high Pacific coast water levels this year with the seasonal high tides called “king tides” has sparked alarm from weather experts, who have warned that the most dangerous flooding is likely to occur if a strong winter storm with heavy wind and rain hits areas of the coast at the same time as the high tide’s peak.
So far, it seems like California has avoided the worst of that risk during the November king tide period. But the amplified king tides will return twice more, around late December and then in late January, in periods where big winter storms remain likely.

Benjamin Netanyahu called for his trial to be ended "immediately"
Judges in Israel have suggested prosecutors drop bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially handing the caretaker prime minister a boost as he fights for his political survival.
The judges told the attorney general that there was little chance of conviction in the first of three cases he is facing, in which he is accused of granting government favours in exchange for positive media coverage.
They also questioned whether his actions amounted to criminal conduct in a second corruption case, and suggested prosecutors seek a plea deal in a third.
Netanyahu has consistently denied the allegations against him and called on Wednesday for the trial to be ended "immediately".
"Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family, my son," he said in a televised statement.
Netanyahu was first charged in 2019, but court proceedings have been prolonged in part by the recent Israel-Gaza war.
The case now under serious doubt, known as Case 4,000, concerns an alleged "reciprocal arrangement" between Netanyahu and the controlling shareholder in Israel's biggest telecoms company. Both denied any wrongdoing.
In a highly unusual step, a judging panel at the Jerusalem District Court summoned Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara on Wednesday to express their concerns.
"The chances of conviction are low – to an extent that warrants reconsidering the matter," Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told her, Israeli media reported.
The judges also cast doubt on whether Netanyahu's actions, which are subject to a second case – concerning another alleged quid-pro-quo with another media baron, known as Case 2,000 – met the threshold for criminality.
While they left open the possibility of a conviction in the third case: Case 1,000, which alleges Netanyahu acted for the benefit of an Australian billionaire after being gifted cigars and champagne by him.
However, the judges told the attorney general that, in the public interest, there needed to be a "rethink" in how the trial should move forward, Israeli media report.
Baharav-Miara said she would consider the judges' recommendations.
It has been six years since Netanyahu became Israel's first sitting prime minister to face a criminal trial.
He has always claimed to be the victim of a political witch-hunt and said on Wednesday that the "fabricated cases" against him were now falling apart.
The cases have continued to progress in court while Netanyahu remained in power throughout the war in Gaza, though judges agreed to reduce the number of hearings due to security concerns around the conflict.
The accusations against him have rocked Israeli politics, fuelling already deep divisions. His trial has coincided with controversial, far-reaching judiciary reforms by Netanyahu's government.
For his opponents, Netanyahu's fear of prison has distorted his decision-making as prime minister and made him especially dependent on his far-right coalition partners to remain in power.
This latest development will give a boost to Netanyahu, whose political opponent Gadi Eisenkot is currently attempting to form a coalition government after an inconclusive general election last month.
While Netanyahu's parliamentary bloc won more seats than that of his rival, both fell short of an outright majority. Israel's president has offered Eisenkot the first chance to form a new administration.
Netanyahu remains subject to an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza, which he also denies.

Meteorologists have warned that the king tide could pair with high surf to bring historic surges to parts of the state.
California and other parts of the United States West Coast have experienced record-high water levels, causing flooding, destruction and dangerous waves.
On Wednesday, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) announced that the fishing community of Charleston, Oregon, notched its highest-ever coastal water level, roughly 1.12 metres above the mean high water level.
Other NOAA stations recorded some of their highest water levels on record, including San Diego, Los Angeles and Santa Barbara, all on the southern California coast.
Further north, the L-shaped municipal pier in Pacifica, a city south of San Francisco, crumbled into the surf after a wave as tall as its platform crashed into it.
In a video on social media, bystanders could be heard voicing astonishment at the sight. “Oh my god, it’s gone. Oh my god,” one person said.
The pier had faced multiple closures in recent years, as seawater weakened its concrete structure, but experts say this week’s conditions were more dangerous than normal.
The high coastal water levels were spurred by a combination of factors, including a phenomenon popularly known as king tides.
The term is applied to the highest tides of the year, created when both the sun and the moon are aligned to create a larger-than-normal tidal bulge, pulling the water with their combined gravitational force.
The king tides have been exacerbated by the El Nino weather pattern as well as human-fuelled climate change.
While El Nino is a regular occurrence, this year’s edition is projected to be stronger than normal, according to forecasters, leading to record-warm waters off the Pacific coast. That warming, in turn, helps churn up powerful storms that contribute to waves battering the shoreline.
San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie announced on Wednesday that his city had made it through the worst of this week’s surge with flooding and waves up to 9 metres, but he warned of more king tides to come.
“The last two weeks have been an important reminder to get prepared for the rest of El Nino season. We’re expecting more king tides in December and January,” he wrote on social media. “We need to take these events seriously, prepare ahead of future storms, and stay alert.”

The judges’ recommendations came as Israel’s longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival.
Israel’s caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for an immediate end to his long-running corruption trial after judges cast doubt on the charges and recommended dropping a case in which he is accused of bribery.
Netanyahu on Wednesday said the “fabricated cases” against him were falling apart, in a televised statement at the Israeli parliament.
Meanwhile, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s parliamentary bloc voted in favour of conducting an independent investigation into the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack.
The judges’ recommendations came as Israel’s longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival after inconclusive October 27 elections.
Eisenkot, who is Netanyahu’s main rival, has been tasked with forming a government, and if Netanyahu is no longer prime minister, he would lose his leverage to avoid a potential jail sentence.
“Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family,” Netanyahu said in his speech.
“Ten years of incitement to hatred that wounds the soul. Who will give those years back to us?”
During a hearing in Jerusalem on Wednesday regarding three corruption cases against Netanyahu, judges recommended dropping one, reconsidering another and suggested resolving the third through an agreement, Israeli media reported.
In Case 4000, in which Netanyahu is accused of bribery, fraud and breach of trust, judges indicated there was little chance of a conviction.
That case is considered to be the most serious Netanyahu faces and involves him allegedly offering regulatory favours for a telecoms company in exchange for favourable media coverage.
Netanyahu is alleged to have negotiated with Shaul Elovitch, the controlling shareholder of Israeli telecommunications giant Bezeq, to get positive coverage on his Walla news site in exchange for policies benefitting Bezeq.
On Wednesday, Israeli media reported Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman saying that proving the bribery charge in that case faced “considerable difficulties”.
Netanyahu, who has been in power on and off for three decades, has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing and denounced the cases as a politically motivated plot against him.
He is the first sitting Israeli prime minister to stand trial.
Israel’s Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara, who was unusually summoned to the hearing on Wednesday, said she would consider the judges’ recommendations and was ready for either a verdict or a plea deal.
In Case 2000, Netanyahu is accused of fraud and breach of trust over an alleged deal with the owner of Yediot Aharonot for favourable coverage in exchange for curbs on rival newspaper Israel Hayom. Judges on Wednesday questioned whether his actions constituted a crime and recommended reconsidering the case.
In Case 1000, Netanyahu is accused of fraud and breach of trust over allegedly accepting luxury gifts from wealthy individuals in exchange for favours. Judges recommended reaching an agreement to conclude the case.
Netanyahu’s right-wing allies cheered the court’s recommendations and demanded the trial be brought to an end.
“After years of persecution against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the time has come to put an end to a trial that was flawed from the outset,” Israel Katz, who is the defence minister in Netanyahu’s caretaker government, wrote on X.
During his most recent term, which started in late 2022, Netanyahu proposed far-reaching judicial reforms that critics say sought to weaken the courts.
With coalition negotiations under way, Eisenkot’s camp is already trying to start unravelling some of the Netanyahu-era judicial reforms in parliament.
The presidential contender is expected to meet Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday evening.
His centrist Yashar party said a day earlier that it had agreed to sign a coalition pact with Israel Our Home party after a meeting with its leader Avigdor Lieberman, the first alliance of its kind since the election.
Lieberman has ruled out forming a coalition with Arab-led parties that could hand them a majority in parliament. That has frustrated Democrats chief Yair Golan, who has been pushing Eisenkot to reach a deal with parties representing Israel’s 21 percent Arab minority to make good on his campaign promise to bring down Netanyahu.
The Israeli parliament’s preliminary approval on Wednesday of a probe into the country’s failures prior to the October 7 attack dealt a blow to Netanyahu, who has repeatedly opposed the move.
The vote was the first of four needed ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠to pass a law establishing a state commission to investigate the Hamas attack.
The parliament also voted in favour of a bill seeking to impose term limits on prime ministers and restrict them from serving while under criminal indictment, seemingly taking aim at Netanyahu.
Eisenkot also faced a new challenge on Tuesday after the left-wing Democrats suspended coalition talks, further complicating his potential path to power.
The Yashar party leader has until December 6 to form a government under a 28-day mandate, though he could ask for a 14-day extension. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would have an opportunity to do so. If no one is able to form a government, another election will be held next year.

Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says.
Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening.
Footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.
Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.
The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead.
The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation.
It then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire, the state-owned newspaper says.
Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas and often run-down infrastructure making incidents more common, the response to which is often complicated by slow emergency response times and locally improvised rescue efforts, even in the sprawling Egyptian capital.
Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished, as emergency services blocked off entry routes.
Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished
The tanker crossed the highway's central reservation before overturning and bursting into flames, local media report
The health ministry said 39 ambulances had been dispatched to respond to the fire, while it posted images of Egypt's health minister overseeing the treatment of the injured at one of Cairo's hospitals.
Road collisions are also common in Egypt, often attributed to lax maintenance and the widespread flouting of traffic laws.
Nearly 6,000 people died on Egypt's roads last year, official figures show, a rise of several hundred on the previous year's total.
Emergency responders have since cleared the highway and allowed it to reopen, state broadcaster NMA reports.
A bulldozer could earlier be seen at the scene clearing the burnt-out wrecks of cars.

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art:
Manchester United were held to a draw in a chaotic and controversial Champions League encounter with Sporting in Lisbon with Mauricio Pochettino denied a first win as United head coach despite his side turning around a first-half deficit.
They were behind at the break after goalkeeper Senne Lammens conceded from a penalty he gave away – having saved another just minutes before.
United then had a goal disallowed before scoring a penalty of their own through Bruno Fernandes, who then put them in front with the help of a large divot on the pitch.
There was more drama as Lammens dropped the ball for Sporting's equaliser before Pochettino's side had what they thought was a winner ruled out.
Polish referee Szymon Marciniak was at the centre of much of the drama with midfielder Youri Tielemans sent off in stoppage time.
Lammens saved a poor penalty from Sporting's Luis Suarez, given after Lisandro Martinez left a leg out which caught Geny Catamo.
The Belgium keeper got down to hold on to Suarez's low effort which looked set to be a huge boost for the underperforming United number one.
Pochettino's whirlwind week ends with optimism and frustration
Lammens went from hero to zero in the space of 76 seconds as he rushed out of his goal and took out Maxi Araujo in the United box.
Noussair Mazraoui was caught out by a ball over the top but it was reckless from Lammens and this time Suarez buried the spot-kick.
Former United midfielder Owen Hargreaves told TNT Sports: "There is no way Senne Lammens can get there. Just stay in the goal."
Amad Diallo thought he had equalised for United before half-time when he headed in after his first attempted was turned on to the cross bar.
However, referee Marciniak blew his whistle for a foul against Youri Tielemans.
Replays showed Tielemans won the ball and pulled out of the challenge after he played the ball through to Amad.
BBC Sport's Dale Johnson: "Marciniak believed that Goncalo Inacio had been fouled by Youri Tielemens on the edge of the area as the Manchester United midfielder played a pass through.
"Rather than immediately blow his whistle, Marciniak held off to let the move play out.
"But when Diallo hit the bar with his first effort, Marciniak blew his whistle.
"Play was dead at that point, so when Diallo then nodded the rebound over the line the VAR was locked out.
"However, the chances that the VAR would have intervened were very slim.
"Tielemens, who was booked, caught Inacio's foot under his body sliding to make the pass, causing the Sporting defender's ankle to buckle."
Former Manchester United midfielder Ashley Young said on BBC Radio 5 Live: "It's an absolute disgrace. I don't know how the referee is seeing that Tielemans has kicked the player.
"On first viewing, I thought his foot must have hit him on the follow through but when you look at it again, Tielemans actually tries to take his foot away.
"He doesn't touch him because he knows the midfielder is coming towards him.
"It is one of the worst decisions I've seen with a referee giving that decision."
United got back on level terms after a foul on Martinez in the Sporting area by Eduardo Quaresma led to a penalty. Bruno Fernandes converted.
Former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha told BBC Sport: "Martinez wins that penalty, but it is a penalty."
United took the lead with two quick-fire goals but in bizarre circumstances as Fernandes' speculative strike looked like it would be easily collected by Kaique Pereira only to hit a divot on the pitch and fly up past the Sporting goalkeeper.
Former Rangers striker Ally McCoist on TNT Sports: "I think it hits a divot and it jumps over the goalkeeper! That is absolutely incredible."
Hargreaves added on TNT Sports: "Unbelievable. It is like a golf divot. There are holes in this pitch absolutely everywhere.
"Bruno Fernandes created a divot, does he get an assist for that?"
Lammens made another error, spilling a high ball under little pressure from Suarez. The Sporting striker then reacted quickly to find the target with an overhead kick to make it 2-2, the goal given after a quick VAR check.
McCoist: "I am baffled because the forward does what you expect him to do.
"The goalkeeper, instead of concentrating on the ball, he thinks about the player."
United thought they had taken the lead as Sporting keeper Kaique appeared to push the ball into his own net from a Fernandes corner.
However, after a VAR intervention, the 'goal' was then disallowed for a foul on the goalkeeper by Patrick Dorgu.
Onuoha: "First that was an absolutely disastrous goal for United to concede for the equaliser. it comes from a nothing ball into the box, too.
"For the United goal that has just been ruled out, the keeper has pushed it into his own net before Dorgu has touched him."
Young added on BBC Radio 5 Live: "The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me.
"If a referee is on the pitch and being sent to the screen, if he's given the goal then stand by your decision."
Midfielder Tielemans was then sent off for a late challenge on Sergi Altimira. The Belgium international's second yellow compounds the controversial one he received in the first half.
United have now received five red cards in all competitions this season - two more than any other Premier League side.
Young added: "The referee's performance was just simply 'wow'.
"The decisions that he gave. Youri Tielemans getting booked to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking and it should have been an equalising goal.
"His decision-making today is nothing more than a disgrace."

There will also be a Champions League Match of the Day on BBC One on Wednesday, from 22:40 to 00:00.

A crushing 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend, leaving United 19th, was a disastrous first game at the helm for Pochettino after replacing Michael Carrick.
Pochettino brought Harry Maguire into the three-man defence as he shuffled his pack, as well as starting Joshua Zirkzee in place of the suspended Matheus Cunha.
Neither side took many risks in the opening stages, with few chances of note until the game burst into life midway through the first half as United lost control.
Lisandro Martinez brought down Geny Catamo in the area and Sporting were awarded a penalty.
The hosts blew their chance from the spot, with Suarez’s scuffed effort easily saved by Lammens, but the Red Devils gave away another spot kick just a couple of minutes later.
Goalkeeper Lammens came flying off his line and clattered Maxi Araujo, and this time Colombian striker Suarez made no mistake from the spot.
United thought they had equalised when Amad Diallo hit the crossbar and then nodded home the rebound, but the goal was disallowed to their dismay.
Youri Tielemans was ruled to have fouled Goncalo Inacio, although he seemed to win the ball, upsetting United further after Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool on Sunday that was later rescinded.
Fernandes pulled United level early in the second half from the spot after Eduardo Quaresma brought down Martinez.
The former Sporting playmaker calmly stroked his penalty beyond the dive of Kaique Pereira into the bottom left corner.
Fernandes said on the eve of the game he had stopped contract talks because he wanted to focus on helping United improve their form after a dire start to the season.
The midfielder soon had his second goal, with the help of a bizarre bounce off a divot on the pitch.
Fernandes’s low effort from distance seemed bound for Pereira’s hands, but suddenly bounced up off a patch of uneven turf and fortuitously over the goalkeeper’s head.
The Portugal international bent a free-kick narrowly off target as he looked to complete his hat-trick.
Lammens saved well from Sergi Altimira to protect United’s lead as Sporting battled to find an equaliser.
It eventually came from a howler from Lammens, who failed to claim a cross dropping out of the sky, spilling the ball in front of Suarez, who produced a hooked acrobatic effort to score.
Moments later United had the ball in the net at the other end after another goalkeeping error by Pereira, who mishandled Fernandes’s corner, pushing the ball into his own net.
However, what would have been the winner was disallowed for an elbow by Patrick Dorgu on the goalkeeper, a decision the visitors were also unhappy about.

Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain held to 2-2 draw by Roma as injury-ravaged squad struggle.
Donyell Malen’s penalty gave Roma a 2-2 draw away to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday, as the injury-hit reigning champions saw their perfect record in this season’s competition come to an end.
Malen stroked in from the spot in the 78th minute on a bitterly cold and wet night at the Parc des Princes, giving Roma a welcome point after their collapse from two goals up to lose 3-2 at Manchester United last time out.
Roma had earlier taken the lead through Mario Hermoso, only for Illia Zabarnyi to equalise before substitute Ousmane Dembele put PSG briefly in front with a penalty of his own.
The result ends PSG’s perfect record in this season’s league phase, and halts a run of 12 consecutive wins in all competitions for Luis Enrique’s team.
They fall two points behind Real Madrid, who are now clear at the top of the standings as the only side still with a 100 percent record after five matches.
It is only a minor setback for PSG in their quest to finish in the top eight of the 36-team table, and therefore qualify directly for the last 16 without having to go through the playoff round like in the last two campaigns.
But the Parisians could have done with the boost of a victory as they come to terms with the loss of the outstanding Desire Doue, who may not play again this season after rupturing the ACL in his right knee last weekend.
Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, another of their outstanding attacking players, recently succumbed to the same injury, while Dembele has been struggling for fitness, too, and PSG’s prospects of winning a third straight Champions League title are undoubtedly diminished as a result.
Dembele’s presence on the bench at kickoff meant that none of PSG’s five top scorers from last season was in their line-up here, with the others either injured or having departed in the case of Bradley Barcola and Goncalo Ramos.
Meanwhile, Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini raised eyebrows by leaving Malen out of his starting XI. The Dutchman is running at an average of more than a goal a game this season and netted four against Parma last weekend.
However, Roma have been in prolific form in general, netting 26 goals in their last seven matches before arriving in the French capital.
They went ahead inside five minutes here as Matias Soule cut the ball back from the byline and Spanish defender Hermoso was on hand to convert.
Roma had blown even more promising leads already this season, though, losing 4-3 at home to Real Madrid after leading 3-1 with eight minutes left, and then going down 3-2 at Old Trafford despite being 2-0 ahead at half-time.
Ukrainian defender Zabarnyi levelled just after the half-hour mark as he found space at the near post to head in Senny Mayulu’s corner.
Evan Ndicka headed just off-target for Roma late in the first half, and Niccolo Pisilli forced a good stop from Matvei Safonov early in the second half.
Joao Neves then headed agonisingly wide for PSG as he arrived unmarked in the area to meet a Nuno Mendes cross, before Dembele was introduced for the hosts in place of the ineffective Ferran Torres.
Moments after that, PSG won a penalty when Achraf Hakimi stormed into the Roma box only to be pulled down by Wesley.
The French side had missed four penalties in the Champions League since the start of last season, but Dembele did score in the final against Arsenal in May.
He kept a cool head to convert his fifth goal of the campaign, but PSG could not make it five straight Champions League wins this season.
Malen entered the fray for Roma midway through the second half and looked on as Dembele was denied a brilliant solo goal by a Mile Svilar save.
Roma then won a penalty following a VAR check after Vitinha blocked a Soule shot with a raised hand in the box.
Up stepped Malen to score his 17th goal of a prolific campaign, boosting Roma’s hopes of reaching the knockout phase.

Andy Taylor, whose guitar riffs helped shape Duran Duran's distinctive sound and propel the British band to global fame in the 1980s, has died aged 65 after a long battle with prostate cancer, the band and his family said Wednesday.
Andy Taylor, the former guitarist with new wave pop group Duran Duran, has died after a "long and courageous battle with prostate cancer", the band and his family said on Instagram late Wednesday. He was 65.
"Andy passed away peacefully at home, surrounded by his family on Monday 23rd November," they said in a joint statement.
Taylor's rock- and funk-inspired riffs drove the British band's dancefloor hits such as "Girls on Film" and "Rio", helping it to define the sound of the 1980s.
Frontman Simon Le Bon was the face of the band, but Taylor's jangling, syncopated guitar lines helped forge its distinctive sound, fusing punk rock and dance influences to make it one of the leaders of the UK "New Romantic" movement.
The band enjoyed huge success in the 1980s, with their popularity in the United States compared to Beatlemania.
They have sold more than 100 million records , had 30 top 40 singles in their native UK and 21 top 40 hits in the US charts.
Best known for timeless hits such as "Rio", and "Hungry Like the Wolf", the band were also one of the first to harness the advent of the music video, to burnish a sophisticated and seductive image.
Taylor was born on the coast near Newcastle, northeast England, on February 16, 1961 and learned the guitar aged 11.
"To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather," his wife, Tracey, said on the Instagram post.
"He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first," she added.
Duran Duran added that Taylor had been there from the beginning of the band's story and had had "an unshakeable belief in what we could become".
"He brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music," they said. "His playing drove the songs that took us around the world."
Taylor joined Duran Duran in 1980, travelling from Tyneside to the band's base in Birmingham, central England, in response to an advert in a music magazine.
The group released its debut album a year later, with first single "Planet Earth" peaking at number 12.
But it was their third single, "Girls on Film", accompanied by a raunchy video featuring topless women mud wrestling, that catapulted Duran Duran to global fame.

Kilmar Abrego García, a Salvadoran man whose wrongful deportation from the United States put him at the centre of a controversy over US President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown, arrived in Madrid on Wednesday.
His case became a focal point in the debate over Trump's mass deportation policy in 2025, raising concerns about migrants' rights to challenge deportation orders and the administration's compliance with court rulings.
Wearing sunglasses and a baseball cap, Abrego García made his way to a vehicle at Madrid airport without speaking to reporters gathered at the scene, according to AFP journalists.
"While details remain private, Kilmar is planning on hosting various international speaking engagements, with stops planned in different countries," We Are CASA, a US immigrant advocacy group which has been supporting him, said in a statement.
The Salvadoran ultimately left the United States voluntarily on a commercial flight bound for Spain.
"I am leaving happy, I am leaving with my freedom," he said in a statement released by We Are CASA.
The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) confirmed his departure from the country in a statement, in which it labelled Abrego García a "trafficker, wife beater, gang member, and child predator."
"We are delighted to announce that Kilmar Abrego Garcia has self-deported from the United States to Spain," said Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, quoted in the statement.
His lawyers, for their part, welcomed the fact that their client had been able to leave "on his own terms" after his long-running dispute with the US immigration authorities.
One of his legal representatives, Simón Sandoval-Moshenberg, said the departure brought an end to a deportation campaign he described as "retaliation". He also stressed that the move to Spain is temporary and that Abrego García, who is married to a US citizen, hopes to return to the United States once Donald Trump leaves the White House.
His case began in March 2025, when federal agents arrested Abrego García in the street. Days later he was deported to El Salvador and sent to the Terrorism Confinement Centre (CECOT), a controversial maximum-security mega-prison built on the orders of President Nayib Bukele and intended to house alleged members of criminal gangs.
The deportation went ahead even though there was a court order expressly prohibiting his deportation to El Salvador, where he had received threats from armed groups before leaving the country. The US government itself later acknowledged that it had been "a mistake", although it initially resisted facilitating his return.
Back in the United States, Abrego García reported having suffered beatings, sleep deprivation and psychological torture during the almost three months he was held in CECOT.
The legal battle reached the US Supreme Court, which ordered the Trump administration to facilitate his return. The authorities eventually brought him back to the country, although they did so in the context of a criminal investigation that led to an indictment over his alleged involvement in a migrant-smuggling network.
However, a federal judge ultimately dismissed all the charges, ruling that the indictment was in fact motivated by a desire to retaliate against the Salvadoran for having opposed his deportation.
As the criminal case progressed, the US government continued trying to deport him from the country. The authorities considered sending him to Uganda, Ghana and Eswatini, but failed to secure agreement from those countries to receive him. Meanwhile, Abrego García applied for asylum to prevent his deportation.
The dispute became one of the most high-profile cases under Trump's immigration policy and highlighted the differences between the executive and judicial branches over the limits of presidential powers regarding deportations.
Throughout the process, the US president and several members of his administration publicly accused the Salvadoran of belonging to Mara Salvatrucha, also known as MS-13, as well as of human trafficking and assaulting his wife, all allegations that were echoed in the statement published on Tuesday by the DHS announcing his departure from the country.
However, these accusations were called into question by the courts. In fact, federal judge Paula Xinis, who oversaw part of the litigation in Maryland, went so far as to open a contempt-of-court inquiry against some of the prosecutors involved in the case for allegedly repeatedly disobeying her orders.
Now, with Madrid as his first stop, Abrego García plans to travel to other countries to take part in various events and speak about his experience, according to Sandoval-Moshenberg.

The Ukrainian General Staff says its forces struck an airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region east of Moscow.
Ukrainian forces have hit a major Russian military base east of Moscow, damaging five aircraft used to launch missiles and bombs, according to the Ukrainian General Staff.
Ukraine struck the Savasleyka airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region, the General Staff said on Wednesday, adding that three MiG-31 jets were used to fire hypersonic missiles and two Su-34 fighter-bombers were damaged.
Russia did not immediately comment on the report by the General Staff, which said the Savasleyka airbase had been hit in the latest long-range attacks aimed at crippling Moscow’s war effort .
The operation followed a series of high-profile strikes by Ukrainian forces in recent days in which two Russian ships were hit in Libyan waters and a Russian vessel was struck in the Gulf of Finland .
Last week, Ukraine destroyed the road portion of Russia’s prized bridge to the Crimea peninsula after consecutive attacks.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and fighting has continued despite a renewed US-backed push to end what has become Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.
Kyiv is trying to dent Moscow’s military might as it struggles under a renewed campaign of attacks on its energy system and mounting Russian strikes on front-line cities.
Ukrainian forces are hunting Russian ballistic-missile launchers used to carry out many of those attacks, striking 16 over the past several months, Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said this week.
Renewed Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian oil refineries’ processing volumes by 45 percent since late October, industry sources said this month. Kyiv has said it will stop striking Russian energy targets only when Moscow does the same.

Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred
A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.
The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.
State media reported that the fire broke out when the fuel truck overturned. The stretch of the highway where it occurred was in Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, the health ministry said.
At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video showed firefighters working to put out the fire spreading among the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene.
Ahmed Sameer, who was stuck in traffic as the road was blocked after the accident, saw the fuel truck and many cars on fire. He said he saw at least eight bodies being removed from burned cars.
“It was a huge fire, the cars got stuck together because of the fire,” he said, describing the fear and panic that followed. “It was a shocking scene.”
The Egyptian president, Abdel Fatah al-Sisi, expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The public prosecutor’s office said DNA investigations were under way to identify the victims.
The health minister, Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that he would head to the scene. He said the death toll was preliminary, raising concerns it could rise further.
Deadly traffic incidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record. Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.
In January, 21 people were killed and 16 were injured in a multicar pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.

At least 31 people were killed and 15 injured when a fuel truck overturned and burst into flames on a busy highway in Cairo on Wednesday, engulfing nearby vehicles, Egyptian authorities said.
A fire erupted in Egyptian capital Cairo on Wednesday killing at least 31 people, the health ministry said, after a fuel truck reportedly overturned on a packed highway.
AFP footage showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital's Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists sounded their horns and scrambled to get away. Surrounding buildings appeared to escape the flames.
State media reported that the fire broke out when a truck loaded with fuel overturned on Cairo's Ring Road -- a crowded highway linking different parts of the capital -- and burst into flames, engulfing nearby vehicles.
The health ministry said 39 ambulances were sent to the scene and 15 people were taken to hospital with injuries, four of them in critical condition.
"The scene was terrifying," Abdel Rahman Khalil told AFP, saying he arrived shortly after the crash and saw the overturned fuel truck engulfed in flames.
AFP images showed a grisly aftermath with cars burned out, as firefighters doused the truck's wreckage.
Egypt's public prosecutor said an investigation had been opened and DNA tests were being carried out to identify badly burned victims.
The health ministry said it had raised its emergency alert level and Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar had travelled to the scene and nearby hospitals.
The health minister's spokesman told state-linked al-Qahera News that "the Ring Road has been reopened, and the remnants of the accident have been cleared."
Footage carried by Al-Qahera News showed the charred truck's wreckage being removed, while traffic partially resumed around it.
A spokesperson for the Egyptian Cabinet told local media that Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly had ordered an investigation into the causes of the accident.
He said the government was awaiting a full clarification before determining "future measures regarding the transport of petroleum products and ensuring safety and security during such transport operations".
Egypt, with its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, has suffered several deadly fires in recent years.
Fire escapes, smoke detectors and alarms are rare and in many areas, warrens of narrow roads make it hard for fire engines to reach disaster sites.
Car crashes are also common, and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted.
Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt's state statistics agency.
The year before, more than 5,200 road deaths were recorded across the country, according to authorities.
In August, at least 18 people, many of them teenagers, were killed in northern Egypt when two pick-up trucks carrying agricultural day-labourers crashed.

Galatasaray 'dan ayrıldıktan sonra yeni takımı merak edilen Mauro Icardi için Almanya 'dan dikkat çeken bir iddia geldi. Hücum hattında sakatlıklarla boğuşan Bayern Münih'in gündeminde kısa vadeli çözümler yer alıyor. Alman basınına göre Arjantinli golcü, bu arayışta adı öne çıkan isimlerden biri oldu.
Bayern Münih, 20 Kasım'daki Köln karşılaşmasında yıldız golcüsü Harry Kane'i sakatlığa kurban verdi. Sendesmoz bağı kopan ve ameliyat olan İngiliz futbolcunun 3-4 ay sahalardan uzak kalması beklenirken, benzer bir sakatlık yaşayan Ismael Saibari'nin de ocak ayının sonlarında dönebileceği ifade ediliyor. İki ismin yokluğu, Alman devinde hücum hattına yapılacak takviyeleri tartışmaya açtı.
Alman basınında yer alan habere göre Bayern Münih, sakatlık sorunlarını aşmak için Mauro Icardi'yi geçici bir seçenek olarak değerlendirebilir. Kulübün devre arasında yüksek bonservis ödeyeceği pahalı bir transfer yerine kısa vadeli bir çözümü tercih edebileceği belirtilirken, sezon sonuna kadar yapılacak bir anlaşma düşük riskli bir hamle olarak görülüyor. Arjantinli golcünün serbest statüde bulunması ve tecrübesi de elini güçlendiren unsurlar arasında gösteriliyor.
33 yaşındaki santrfor, Galatasaray formasıyla geçirdiği son sezonda yalnızca 12 maça ilk 11'de başlamasına rağmen Süper Lig'de 14 gole ulaştı. Sarı kırmızılı ekipte dört sezon forma giyen Icardi, çıktığı 134 resmi maçta 77 gol ve 25 asistlik bir performans ortaya koydu. Arjantinli futbolcu, Galatasaray'dan ayrılmasının ardından bonservisi elinde bulunuyor.
Bayern daha önce de benzer bir formülden verim almıştı. Robert Lewandowski'nin yedeği olarak transfer edilen Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting, 2020 ile 2024 yılları arasında Münih ekibinde kalarak takımın önemli yedeklerinden biri oldu. Alman basınındaki bir başka habere göre New York Red Bulls forması giyen ve sözleşmesi aralık ayında sona erecek olan 37 yaşındaki golcü de yeniden gündemdeki adaylar arasında yer alıyor.

Russia launched scores of drones at energy and civilian targets across Ukraine overnight on Wednesday, killing at least seven people in six regions, authorities said.
The attack involved 112 Shahed, Gerbera and Parodiya decoy drones, of which 88 were shot down or neutralised, Ukraine's air force said.
One person was killed in Bila Tserkva in Kyiv region, where the strike damaged critical infrastructure, an Epicentr shopping centre and a Nova Poshta postal branch, local authorities said.
One person was killed and seven injured in Kharkiv region after a strike hit a minibus on a highway, regional governor Oleh Synehubov said. Two people aged 76 and 69 were killed and another wounded in Sumy region.
Two people were killed in Odesa region on Tuesday evening — a 41-year-old and a 17-year-old — and one person was killed and three wounded in Zhytomyr region. Casualties were also reported in Chernihiv and Donetsk regions.
Russian forces struck a Naftogaz gas production facility in the Poltava region, the acting head of the company Serhiy Fedorenko said.
A fire broke out and the facility suspended operations. "This is not the first such attack and, unfortunately, not the last," Fedorenko said, adding that Russia was deliberately targeting gas production "to deprive Ukrainians of heat in winter."
Energy facilities in the Dnipropetrovsk region were also hit, triggering emergency power cuts across several districts.
A significant number of consumers lost power in Zaporizhzhia region, Zaporizhzhyaoblenergo head Andriy Stasevskyi said. More than 9,000 customers were left without electricity in Odesa region following Tuesday evening's attacks, regional governor Oleh Kiper said.
The energy company DTEK reported a large-scale strike on one of its thermal power plants, causing serious damage and forcing it to stop generating electricity. DTEK did not specify the location, noting it was the third large-scale strike on its plants in November.
Ukrainian drones simultaneously struck three Russian oil refineries overnight, hitting plants in Samara and Rostov regions, according to Ukrainian monitoring sources.
Two refineries in Samara region — the Kuibyshev and Syzran plants, both part of Rosneft — were struck, with fires breaking out at both facilities.
Regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev confirmed the attack but did not name the facilities, saying one person was killed, power had been cut in several districts and a number of schools would operate on an adjusted schedule.
Regional authorities said 145 drones were shot down over the Samara region. Euronews could not independently verify these claims.
The Syzran refinery has a processing capacity of 8.5 million tonnes of oil per year and produces petrol, diesel, aviation kerosene, fuel oil and bitumen.
The Kuibyshev refinery has a primary processing capacity of 8.8 million tonnes per year. Ukraine last struck the Syzran plant on 15 September. The Kuibyshev refinery was also struck that month.
The third refinery struck overnight was the Novoshakhtinsk plant in Rostov region. Regional governor Yuri Slyusar confirmed the attack, saying a combined strike of more than 50 drones and missiles lasted six hours before the plant suspended operations.
Russian oil refining volumes have fallen by an estimated 45% since late October, according to analysts.
Ukraine's General Staff also reported overnight strikes on the Savasleyka airbase in Nizhny Novgorod region, which it described as one of Russia's key aviation facilities and the base from which aircraft carrying Kinzhal missiles launch strikes on Ukrainian cities.
According to Kyiv's military, three MiG-31 and two Su-34 aircraft were damaged and would be unable to fly "for some time".
Ukraine destroyed a span of the road section of the Crimean Bridge last week, halting car traffic, though train services have been restored.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strike was a response to Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure, describing deep strikes inside Russia as "long-range sanctions".
Ukraine attacked the bulk carrier Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, claiming it transported military cargo. The following day it struck the Russian corvette Merkury in the Libyan port of Benghazi. Zelenskyy confirmed the warship had been sunk.
On Tuesday, Russia's Vladimir Putin threatened Ukraine with retaliation for its strikes on refineries and complained that Kyiv had not heeded calls from US President Donald Trump to halt attacks on oil processing facilities.
Zelenskyy had said Ukraine was prepared to stop striking Russian refineries only if Moscow halted its attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
